slides.title: Digital Signature
slides.teach: A cryptographic signature created with a private key and verified with the corresponding public key.

course.learn: A cryptographic signature created with a private key and verified with the corresponding public key.

breakdown.explanation: Private key signs; public key verifies.
Signed software, Signed document, Signed email

course.why: It can provide integrity, signer authentication, and non-repudiation.
course.example: A software vendor signs an update with its private key and clients verify the signature with the vendor's public key.
course.exam: Digital signatures do NOT automatically provide confidentiality.

blocks.title: Digital Signatures
blocks.prompt: Recognize the concept, understand why it matters, and identify it in a Security+ scenario.

cards.name: Digital Signature
cards.definition: A cryptographic signature created with a private key and verified with the corresponding public key.

blocks.title: Who signs, who verifies, and what does it prove?
items: The signer uses the private key to create the signature.
Example: A vendor signs an update with its private key.
Others use the corresponding public key to verify the signature.
Example: A client verifies the vendor's signature.
A digital signature proves integrity and origin but does not automatically hide the message.
Example: A signed document may still be readable.
blocks.example: Memory: Private signs · Public verifies · Signature proves integrity/origin, not secrecy.

questions.q: A software vendor wants customers to verify that an update came from the vendor and was not modified. Which solution best fits?
questions.explanation: A digital signature supports integrity and signer authentication.

questions.q: Which key is used to create a digital signature?
questions.explanation: The signer uses the private key to create the signature.

questions.q: Which key is used to verify a digital signature?
questions.explanation: The corresponding public key verifies the signature.

questions.q: Which security properties are most directly associated with digital signatures?
questions.explanation: Digital signatures support integrity, authentication of the signer, and non-repudiation.

questions.q: A document is digitally signed but not encrypted. Which statement is correct?
choices: The signature does not by itself make the document confidential
The signature automatically hides the document contents
The signature replaces the need for hashing
The signature makes the document unavailable to unauthorized users
questions.explanation: Digital signatures do not automatically provide confidentiality.
